historical_references.reference: Jadu was a famous sorcerer and magician in ancient India. He is mentioned in the Mahabharata, an Indian epic, as one of the principal advisors to King Yudhishthira during his exile in the forest. Jadu's magical powers included the ability to create illusions, control animals, and even manipulate the elements. He also possessed the Veda Vyasa's sacred text, the Mahabharata, which he used to impart knowledge to King Yudhishthira.

Another reference to Jadu can be found in the Puranas, a collection of Indian mythological texts. Jadu is mentioned as a great sage and a devotee of Lord Shiva. He is also referred to as the 'King of Magicians' and the 'Lord of Illusions'. According to the legend, Jadu performed severe penance to please Lord Shiva and was granted the boon of invincibility against all kinds of attacks, except those by other sages.
